notes.title: The FINAL FIVE SHAKESPEARE + DCS update!
notes.notes:
[img]https://clan.cloudflare.steamstatic.com/images/33017070/a3690f55b8af0f5dccbcfd45c9c724daf41ba655.gif[/img]
The mad quest to make a game for every Shakespeare play is swiftly reaching its promised end, with the first being Army of Tentacles: [b]Assault on Rainbow Unicorn Island[/b]. After that, maybe we can sleep. 

Two are scheduled for the end of 2024, but the majority of work on those will commence after [b]Dinosaur Cousin Squad[/b] has dropped. We don't yet know when that one will have a Store Page up, but we assume within the next few months. Both games were being prepped while Dinosaur Cousin Squad was being worked on, but DCS progress has hit a few fun new snags, so we might be able to finish before proper level clean-up is set to begin in a few months. 

The final two are set for early and late 2025. One is a collaboration, and the other is another new engine, new genre game..... this time: a tRPG deck builder. In layman's terms, a party based tactical RPG with a card system. We've very recently begun pre-production and asset buy on that one. 

Store pages for at least two of the final four adaptations will be popping up after [b]Rainbow Unicorn Island[/b] drops on the 23rd.

notes.title: AoT Recodes: Bit of a Snag, Bit of an Update
notes.notes:
The newest patch for [b]Army of Tentacles 3[/b] went out a few hours ago. It doesn't have any real changes at all minus a few clean-up thingamabobs.

It's unknown if [b]Army 1[/b] will have the same treatment or not. 

Here's why:
I know that I promised new features or at least updated features for the games, but that was before my health took a turn for the worse. It seems that the surgery I had about a year ago left me with other festering issues that are just now getting around to being addressed, which includes another surgery in exactly one month. 

That + new meds + my current brain fog = I had to hire new contractors to help fix what was broken in the old games, and at this point, [b]Army 3[/b] was able to get back up to working condition.

notes.title: AoT 1 + 3 Redo Update
notes.notes:
[img]https://cdn.cloudflare.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33017070/edb082c327a93622eac8d44ce5ea68cb37c53e71.jpg[/img]

[b]Army of Tentacles 1[/b]'s redo is about 50% complete. All of the side quests are finished. Brain fog is not helping my productivity, but I'm doing about two quests a day, plus a quest a day on [b]Army of Tentacles 2[/b]. 

I know I originally set the release date for February, and then March, but if they both are ready by the end of January, they might be both launching then.

Don't worry. I fully realize my workload as well as my current state of being/mind/health, so it might not happen.

[b]Army of Tentacles 3[/b] is a different story. It's a lot less restrictive than Army 1, both code-wise and VO-wise (because there is no VO). We thought about adding VO to the game, but ruled against it, as that would be money we need for [b]Unicorns[/b] and [b]Dinosaur Cousin Squad[/b], and the game's plot relied on a lack of VO. 

The biggest change to Army 3 is that we are cutting down the number of Arguments for a leaner, faster experience. With the DLCs, Army 3 has a whopping 70 Arguments to Army 1's, what, 20? I don't yet know how that is going to translate into quests yet. Some quests might be merged with others, I don't know yet. A lot of the Arguments were not even related to quests, and those may be the majority that go. Another feature that is going to take some busywork.... Army 3 has a large party, and it'll be interesting to see what skills change, what stay the same, and what have fun new uses.

notes.title: Army of Tentacles 2022, Spooky Cat Girls?: Changes
notes.notes:
[img]https://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33017070/093609f034bbf0c064c59ab751c2d65d3de347b5.png[/img]

Doing things isn't easy. 
Video games are hard, as someone once said I forget who, but it's an actual quote. I think it may be from an executive. I dunno.

Being a niche indie company is hard.

Hired a new writer for [b]Spooky Cat Girls?[/b]'s classroom scenes when it became clear that it would not make a reasonable launch date for October. It was either launch directly before the Halloween sale (and this was hoping Valve would accept the final build on the first submission, never something a designer should bet on) or delay it, and we chose to delay it. We feel December also fits in with the theme of the chosen play.

[b]Super Army of Tentacles[/b] has always been my baby, but it's gone through so many changes, due to gameplay as well as personal reasons, that I feel a disconnect with it. Rather than make a tentpole game that I do not want to make, I handed it off to another team member for a 2023 release. This would be the first Army of Tentacles game not helmed by me, which is exciting as I 100% trust my team and think it is time that we all grow in that fashion. We've been alive almost five-point-something years now.

In the place of [b]Super Army of Tentacles[/b], I plan on making a new, full VN-RPG Army of Tentacles game. I feel much more confident about this one, and it will launch at the same time that [b]Super Army 2022[/b] would have. That will be announced soon, maybe with the other 2022 games. Maybe not. Who knows.

Making games is hard.

notes.title: patch, 9.7.2021
notes.notes:
- ADDED: Content Warning

Added a content warning, as some of the endgame paths can lead to some content. Topics such as abuse. 

Conventions are supposed to be fun, but they are also outlets for our feelings.  Being cooped up all year, only to do this one annual thing where you see all your out-of-country or out-of-state friends and make new connections..... that's powerful.

Sometimes, you end up purging your emotions because it's a safe environment to do so.

So there's a content warning. Some endgame paths lead to purging of said emotions.

notes.title: Midsummer gameplay changes
notes.notes:
[img]https://cdn.cloudflare.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33017070/6814e249d8973330b697bf7d3b4a24783e52bff9.jpg[/img]

So, we're putting the finishing touches on Midsummer, and without going into the gory details, a large chunk of the gameplay was vaporized from existence: the weekly slasher competitions. We still have the endgame slasher segment, and we have changed the game's story to put focus on an endgame segment rather than multiple slasher sections. We feel this is important as an announcement because our store page used to have language directly implying multiple sections throughout the game. 

The silver lining here is that we feel that the focus on a singular slasher section rather than multiple improves the general gameplay and story, as well as the "unique aspect" of such a section existing in the story itself. It was either that or delay the game for something that we now feel would have hurt the gameplay rather than added to it.
